claims.text: Edward Jones: The 10-Q for the period ended September 26, 2025 states financial advisor attrition was 6.1% for the third quarter of 2025, attributing it to a variety of factors including a rise in departures of advisors with tenure of five years or less. Attrition % represents the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end.

Edward Jones: The 10-Q for the period ended June 27, 2025 states financial advisor attrition increased to 6.4% for the second quarter of 2025, primarily due to an increase in retirements, consistent with industry trends.
Edward Jones: The 10-Q for the period ended September 26, 2025 reports attrition of 6.0% for the nine months ended September 26, 2025, versus 5.1% for the nine months ended September 27, 2024.
Edward Jones: The 10-Q for the period ended September 26, 2025 reports attrition of 4.7% for the third quarter of 2024.
Merrill: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), CFO Alastair Borthwick stated that adviser attrition is now at near historic lows, without giving a specific attrition rate figure.

Edward Jones discloses a specific, annualized financial advisor attrition rate (6.1% for the third quarter of 2025), whereas Merrill does not disclose a numeric attrition rate — its CFO only stated that adviser attrition is now at near historic lows without giving a figure. With no numeric rate for Merrill, the two firms' attrition rates cannot be compared or ranked.
